o2.texto: You breathe it all the time. The Martian air is almost all carbon dioxide (CO₂), so you can't breathe it: you have to make your own oxygen.
o2.sube: the MOXIE machine (if you give it energy) and a little bit the plants.
o2.baja: breathing, going on missions (the suit uses oxygen) and making fuel.
o2.real: the MOXIE instrument on the Perseverance rover made oxygen from the CO₂ on Mars.

agua.texto: You need it to drink, water the plants and make fuel. It also protects you from radiation!
agua.sube: the Habitat recycler and the ice in the crater (Rover mission).
agua.baja: drinking, watering, making fuel and filling the shelter walls.
agua.real: on the International Space Station about 98% of the water is recycled.

bateria.texto: Everything in the base runs on electricity. The solar panels make it during the day and the battery stores it.
bateria.sube: clean solar panels and the ship's battery once you repair it.
bateria.baja: MOXIE, life support and the greenhouse. Dust and storms make the panels produce less.
bateria.real: dust covered the panels of the InSight lander and left it without power in 2022.

comida.texto: You have rations from the ship, but they run out. To survive you have to grow food in the greenhouse.
comida.baja: eating every sol. If it's cold, you eat more.
comida.real: ISS astronauts have already grown and eaten lettuce in space.

dosis.texto: It's invisible energy that comes from the Sun and from space. Too much radiation is bad for your body. This bar measures the dose you build up: it never goes down!
dosis.sube: a little every sol, when you walk outside, much more on missions and a lot during solar storms.
dosis.baja: it never goes down. From 45, your suit air lasts less; from 75, you have 1 action less each sol. Protect yourself with the Habitat's water walls, regolith and shields.
dosis.real: Mars has no magnetic field to protect it like Earth does. The Curiosity rover measures radiation with its RAD instrument.

metal.texto: Used to repair the tanks, the heat shield, the engine and to upgrade the recycler.

cables.texto: They carry electricity. You need them for the antenna, the electrical system and the engine.

chips.texto: Tiny computers. The antenna, the shield, the engine and the navigation computer need them.

repuestos.texto: The filter removes the CO₂ you breathe out. When it wears out, change it in the Habitat. If you run out of spares, you can use metal.

combustible.texto: The ship needs fuel to go back to Earth. It's made with oxygen from MOXIE and water. Every kilo of oxygen for fuel is one less to breathe!
combustible.sube: in MOXIE, once you repair the ship's tanks.
combustible.real: NASA is studying how to make the return fuel on Mars so it doesn't have to be brought all the way from Earth.

partes.texto: Your ship has 6 broken parts. Repair them all, fill the fuel and lift off before the launch window closes.

traje.texto: Outside you can't breathe: the Martian air is almost all CO₂. Your suit holds air for a few seconds. When you're outside it runs down; when you go into the Ship (or the pressurized room) it refills.
traje.sube: standing at the door of the Starship V3 or the pressurized room. Refilling uses oxygen from the base's reserve.
traje.real: NASA spacesuits carry their own life support system in the backpack, with oxygen for several hours.

sol.texto: A «sol» is a day on Mars: it lasts 24 hours and 39 minutes. The day moves on by itself from 06:00 to 21:00; at dusk the Mission Council meets. Each sol you have 4 actions (like hours of work). If you're done, press «Sleep now».
sol.real: Earth and Mars line up well for travel roughly every 26 months. That's why you have a time limit.
